heavy-bleeding.title: Heavy bleeding from your vagina
heavy-bleeding.detail: Bleeding that soaks a pad soon after you put it on, or comes with clots, severe pain, dizziness or fainting. Call emergency services.

severe-tummy-pain.title: Severe or constant tummy pain
severe-tummy-pain.detail: Strong pain that doesn't ease with rest, especially with bleeding, a hard tummy, shoulder-tip pain or feeling faint. Call your maternity unit or emergency services now.

pre-eclampsia-signs.title: Severe headache, vision changes or sudden swelling
pre-eclampsia-signs.detail: A headache that won't go away, blurred vision or flashing lights, pain under your ribs, or sudden swelling of your face, hands or feet. These can be signs of pre-eclampsia: call your maternity unit or doctor now.

reduced-movements.title: Baby moving less, or not at all
reduced-movements.detail: Any change to your baby's usual pattern of movements. Call your maternity unit immediately, even at night. Don't wait until tomorrow, and don't rely on a home heartbeat monitor.

waters-before-37-weeks.title: Waters breaking or contractions before 37 weeks
waters-before-37-weeks.detail: A gush or trickle of fluid, or regular tightenings or period-like pains before 37 weeks. Wear a pad, not a tampon, and call your maternity unit now.

fever.title: Fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher
fever.detail: Feeling hot, shivery and very unwell counts too. Infections need quick treatment in pregnancy, so call your doctor or maternity unit today.

breathlessness-chest-pain.title: Sudden breathlessness or chest pain
breathlessness-chest-pain.detail: Struggling to breathe, chest pain or tightness, coughing up blood, or a racing heart with faintness. Call emergency services.

swollen-calf.title: Painful, swollen leg on one side
swollen-calf.detail: Throbbing pain, swelling, warmth or redness in one calf or thigh can be a blood clot. Get seen the same day, or call emergency services if you're also breathless.

fainting.title: Fainting, collapse or a seizure
fainting.detail: Passing out, having a fit, or feeling so dizzy you can't stand, especially with pain or bleeding. Call emergency services.

intense-itching.title: Intense itching, especially of hands and feet
intense-itching.detail: Itching on your palms or soles, often worse at night and without a rash, can be a liver condition called ICP. Call your maternity unit or doctor today for a blood test.

thoughts-of-harm.title: Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby
thoughts-of-harm.detail: You're not alone, and it isn't your fault. Tell someone near you, and call emergency services or a crisis line now if you feel unsafe.

severe-vomiting.title: Vomiting and can't keep fluids down
severe-vomiting.detail: Being sick so much you can't keep food or fluids down for 24 hours, very dark pee, not peeing for 8 hours, or feeling faint. You may need fluids: call your doctor now.
